record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For cross-silo federated learning, what formal privacy guarantees are appropriate when client organizations may control data from many users, may distrust other clients more than the server, and may require local or user-level differential privacy depending on the application?

evidence.quote: This area has not been systematically explored.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cross-silo federated learning setting in which a fixed set of K client organizations (silos) jointly train a model via a central server. Each silo k holds a local dataset D_k consisting of records contributed by n_k end-users (so silo k can be viewed as a collection of user-level data). Communication proceeds in rounds: in each round the server sends a model to a subset of silos, each participating silo computes an update from its local data, and the server aggregates the updates to produce the next model. Assume the following threat model: (i) each silo is honest-but-curious and may attempt to infer information about data held by other silos; (ii) silos trust the server less than they would trust themselves but possibly more or less than they trust other silos; (iii) some applications require protection of individual users (user-level guarantees) whereas others require protection at the level of an entire silo's contribution.

Formulate a formal differential-privacy-style definition (or family of definitions) of privacy that simultaneously captures:

1. A notion of inter-silo privacy: the joint view of any coalition of silos (together with, optionally, the server) should be (ε, δ)-indistinguishable under change of a single user's record, or under change of an entire silo's dataset, depending on the application's required granularity.

2. A configurable trust model in which the server's view and each silo's view may be governed by different privacy parameters (ε_server, ε_silo, δ_server, δ_silo), reducing to local differential privacy when no party is trusted and to central differential privacy when the server is fully trusted.

3. A clear specification of the unit of privacy (single user vs. silo) and of neighboring datasets at the federation level.

Provide such a definition, prove its basic properties (post-processing, composition across rounds and across silos, group privacy with respect to multiple users within one silo), and exhibit a federated training mechanism that satisfies the definition with non-trivial utility guarantees for convex stochastic optimization.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of formalizing appropriate privacy notions for cross-silo federated learning under varied trust models and granularities (user-level vs. silo-level) is highlighted as not systematically explored. Subsequent works (e.g., on inter-silo record-level DP, ISRL-DP, and shuffle-model variants) have proposed partial formalizations and algorithms, but a unified, broadly accepted framework covering all listed trust configurations and granularities does not appear to be established, so the broad problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Differentially Private Federated Learning on Heterogeneous Data / ISRL-DP
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces inter-silo record-level differential privacy (ISRL-DP) addressing one specific trust configuration in cross-silo FL.
status_evidence.claim: Partial formalizations exist (ISRL-DP) but address only specific cases.
